findings_seen.title: The Terminal gateway passes terminal-api's own 401 and 429 straight to the page: a signed-in user is told to sign in again, and quota refusals have no LIMIT_REACHED code and no Retry-After
findings_seen.general_class: An upstream service's status code and error body reused as the gateway's own answer, so an upstream account problem looks like the user's session. The same mechanism appears in PageFiles (429 without Retry-After), in the 3c cut relay route still to be built, and in every page that reads /api/terminal/v1: Terminal live.ts, backtest/src/api/live.ts (/bundle), watchlist/src/api.ts (logos). M260 (OPEN) is the same relay lacking public_data, so both belong in one relay helper.

findings_seen.title: orc-test-runner still holds MARKET_AI_ORC_API_KEY, the Orc key that may name any owner, so the M475 fix is incomplete at the credential level
findings_seen.general_class: A credential retired in code but left in a service's environment. Check every service moved to a narrower key: the workers' TERMINAL_PROXY_KEY now references their service keys (RAILWAY_CHANGELOG.md:6871, :6899); AUDIT_STORE_READER_KEY was deleted from orc-test-runner (:3198). For 3c, the terminal-api gateway key must stay on edge-bff only, because with 3c its owner and admin headers are trusted.

findings_seen.title: EDGE_OWNER may be set to an owner key Orc reserves for the test key; with the switch off EDGE then runs user #1 under it
findings_seen.general_class: An identity boundary that depends on a key namespace: the reserved-key rule covers server-made keys and DB rows but not the configured key. The same applies to EDGE_ADMIN_OWNERS entries and, in 3c, to terminal.subscriber.edge_owner_key made from the switch-off owner.

findings_seen.title: The EDGE gateway's terminal-api account expires 2027-10-25 and nothing tracks the date; at expiry every Terminal call fails, and through the relay above it looks like a sign-out
findings_seen.general_class: A time-limited row holding up a service credential, with no expiry monitoring. 3c's per-owner rows will need an expiry policy too (from the EDGE plan, not a fixed date).

findings_seen.title: PageFiles' shared caches mean 3c's per-owner terminal-api audit and quota would record only the first owner to read each page file
findings_seen.general_class: A shared process cache in front of a per-principal audit or quota. The same question applies to any 3c cut cache in edge-bff and to the screener and backtest caches if per-owner terminal-api audit is extended to them.

findings_seen.title: CONTRACT section 7's Phase 3 Orc capabilities header (X-Saniti-Capabilities: levels, modes, lane, export) is neither built nor recorded as deferred
findings_seen.general_class: A contract clause superseded by a later decision without a record, so the later phase's spec silently drops it.

findings_seen.title: F3: an MFA-passed re-enrolment drops confirmed_at, so a password-only session can enrol its own authenticator and take the admin's second factor
findings_seen.general_class: A security setting replaced in place before its replacement is proved, so the old guarantee lapses when the change starts. Same mechanism to avoid in: the email change (purpose email_change exists in email_codes; Phase 4) if the old address is unlinked before the new one is confirmed; recovery-code regeneration; Phase 4/5 admin actions that end the old subscription or role row before the new one is active. Starting a factor change also needs a fresh proof of the current factor (OWASP MFA cheat sheet), which no route asks for today.

findings_seen.title: F2: password/reset answers 429 LIMIT_REACHED after 20 wrong codes only for an address that has an account (enumeration oracle)
findings_seen.general_class: A per-account limit that answers only when the account exists. The sign-in avoids it by counting every typed login (SIGNIN_LOGIN); register, forgot and code/resend answer the same 202 inside their limits; register/verify needs the registration cookie. To keep in mind for every later unauthenticated route with a per-user limit: the email change (Phase 4), an admin 'resend a code', payment flows by email (Phase 5).

findings_seen.title: F8: anyone who types a login can keep it at the sign-in limit; a reset by email code does not lift it, a stranger can also kill the live reset code and use up the reset emails, and the message promises a one-minute wait
findings_seen.general_class: A limit keyed by a public identifier that anyone can drive to its cap, with no proof-based way out, and whose message understates the wait. Instances: SIGNIN_LOGIN (switch off and on), CODE_USER through reset (20 wrong codes lock an account's codes 24 h, contract-chosen), SEND_EMAIL and the one-live-code rule through forgot. The MFA lock has ways out (N2). Phase 3c's per-owner Terminal quotas are keyed by the session's owner_key, not a typed value, so they are not in this class.

findings_seen.title: F1: throttle keys '<prefix>:<value>' share a scope with caller-typed keys: the login 'change:<user_id>' locks that user's password change, and the address 'register:<email>' uses up <email>'s new-registration limit
findings_seen.general_class: Domain separation by string prefix inside a shared HMAC scope, where another route feeds caller-chosen text into the same scope. Same scope sharing today: CODE_USER ('<user_id>') and MFA_USER ('mfa:<user_id>') in code_user (safe now, neither takes typed text). Any later limit added to an existing scope with a prefix (Phase 4 admin actions, Phase 5 payments) inherits it.

findings_seen.title: F4: registering again in the same browser within the hour replaces the registration cookie, so the code already mailed can no longer finish the first registration
findings_seen.general_class: An answer that always sets a fresh binding cookie when it made nothing orphans the browser's live binding. Instances: register (open), sign-in 401 (fixed N3). Later browser-bound flows (Phase 5 checkout return) must keep the held binding the same way.

findings_seen.title: F5: USERNAME_TAKEN uses none of the code's 5 tries, so one proved code looks up any number of usernames
findings_seen.general_class: A gate whose proof is checked but not counted per answer. The contract puts USERNAME_TAKEN behind the code to stop enumeration; the same applies to any later availability answer behind a code (an email change to a taken address, Phase 4).

findings_seen.title: F6: one registration by another browser plus its resends uses all 10 of the address's daily emails, against the recorded decision N4
findings_seen.general_class: A per-address send budget shared between the address owner and anyone who names the address: registration resends and restarts (here) and password/forgot for an existing account (see F8's probe).

findings_seen.title: F7: the sign-in body caps login at 200 characters while registration accepts emails of up to 254
findings_seen.general_class: Two validators of one value with different bounds; check every field the registration accepts against the sign-in, reset and later admin forms (username 30, email 254, password 256 normalised vs 1024 raw, which errs the safe way).

findings_seen.title: F9: the route-walk test accepts a hook route listed in HOOK_ROUTES whether or not its handler verifies the signature
findings_seen.general_class: A registry membership check standing in for a behavioural guarantee. The payment hooks (CONTRACT 11) are the next routes under the prefix.

findings_seen.title: F10: no consecutive-failure cap per account for the password (NIST SP 800-63B-4 3.2.2: at most 100), while the MFA got one
findings_seen.general_class: Rate limit per identifier but no bound per subscriber account across identifiers and windows; any later login identifier (Google identity, CONTRACT 1) adds another window.

findings_seen.title: The Screener's cached paint shows the last result after the plan lost the Screener (and never asks when the plan only narrowed)
findings_seen.general_class: A browser copy of an answer computed under a principal's entitlements, read again on the strength of the session (or the login) alone instead of on an answer the current plan earned. Every such cache must be keyed by the entitlements version as well as the identity, or confirmed by a gated answer before it is drawn. The Terminal's file cache is safe: it reads only the shas that /bundle announces on that load (rack.ts announced/readVerified), so 3c's cut files are not built on this. The same class: `edge.watchlist.logos` (class browser) keeps the content of the `logos` reference file, the ticke

findings_seen.title: /api/v1/preferences serves and stores the tabs' saved items with no tab capability (D5 bypass through Phase 1's preference store)
findings_seen.general_class: A route that reads or writes another tab's data needs that tab's capability, the M481 C2 1 lesson (the Screener star writing the Watchlist). A generic per-account key/value store carries data of every tab. Which capability a key needs is decided by the key, not by the route, so the registry entry should name its tab and the server should check it per key on GET (filter) and PUT (refuse). The same mechanism applies to any later generic store, such as an admin or usage store.

findings_seen.title: A drawings refusal (403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED) is read as 'account unreachable': the drawing is kept in the browser and the message names a connection failure
findings_seen.general_class: An offline or fallback path that treats a plan refusal like a network failure and carries on locally. Each client fallback must tell CAPABILITY_REQUIRED, PLAN_EXPIRED and LIMIT_REACHED (403/429, isAccessRefusal) apart from status 0/5xx. Layouts and presets do (savedClient's sentence uses accessText); the drawings' listOf does not. Contract 8b 3e lists lock prompts for Flow, Broker, the indicator menu, compare and assets, but not drawings, so 3e as written would miss this. 3c's Terminal data client should keep the same rule for /bundle and /files refusals (live.ts does today).

findings_seen.title: Browser-class keys named after the added series' tickers survive sign-out and a change of user
findings_seen.general_class: A `browser` key family whose key names carry account content: classification by prefix misses user data in the suffix. Checked the other browser families: ml.stats.*, ml.broker.*, ml.fd.*, ml.win.* (window ids bs/acc/inv/fd), ml.draw.*, edge-sources-open:<fixed UI labels> carry no account content. ml.winst.* holds a chosen broker-window period (dates), which is borderline. Any per-ticker or per-item UI state that 3c or 3e adds (for example a dismissed lock prompt per ticker) belongs to the same class.

findings_seen.title: The two-user acceptance test (CONTRACT 13.3) leaves out several owned kinds and every cross-owner write by id
findings_seen.general_class: The 13.3 test lists kinds by hand, while the route table already gives every owned route. A route-derived two-user walk (as the 3a route walk derives capabilities) would cover new routes automatically, 3c's included.

findings_seen.title: Values Phase 2 accepts, or reads as the most restrictive (limit 0), break the 3c x-terminal-capabilities header: terminal-api answers 400 for every Terminal call of the account
findings_seen.general_class: Phase 2 has one value domain per kind, while each consumer has its own narrower domain, so a value the catalog accepts can be out of range for the wire that carries it. The same mechanism reaches the 3c quota limits: a RESTRICTIVE 0 becomes 429 'try again later' with Retry-After 3600, although waiting does not help. It also reaches any later limit or list a worker or service validates (context.limits for the workers, Phase 3e page limits). Another check: JS and Python truthiness treat 0 and [] like 'no limit' (None). 3c uses `is None` (terminal_access.py:82, 91), but every new consumer must do

findings_seen.title: Principal.refusal never answers PLAN_EXPIRED for a list or limit restriction (terminal.tickers, terminal.history_days), which 3c refuses through p.refusal
findings_seen.general_class: The refusal API takes a capability key without the item or amount asked. So any restriction whose 'held' depends on a value (a list member, a number within a limit) cannot follow the PLAN_EXPIRED rule. This covers the 3c refusals (tickers, history), the 3a saved-item caps (LIMIT_REACHED for watchlist, layouts, presets, drawings and backtest.queued_jobs after a lapse), the 3c quota and later limits. Also, CONTRACT 8b '3c in detail' says CAPABILITY_REQUIRED for a ticker outside tickers, which contradicts 8a. The contract needs one sentence that settles it.

findings_seen.title: read_grants hands the same RESTRICTIVE list object to every principal with a malformed list value
findings_seen.general_class: A shared mutable default inside a per-request entitlement object. This applies to any list kind added later and to the 3e mirrors. The front-end limit() returns a filtered copy, which is safe.

findings_seen.title: seed_subscription treats a plan holding '*' = false as the plan that holds every capability
findings_seen.general_class: Code that asks 'which plan holds X' by row existence, after flags started to allow false. The same check is needed in the Phase 4 admin page, the payment adapter's plan lookup and every migration verify that counts '*' holders.

findings_seen.title: Two edge-bff 429 answers lack Retry-After: the page-file quota refusal and the Terminal gateway relay. These are the paths 3c's per-owner Terminal quotas reach the page through
findings_seen.general_class: An edge-bff path that relays or rebuilds another service's refusal (forward_terminal, PageFiles for overview, radar and watchlist, and any 3c relay such as the cut route) drops that service's headers and code, so the contract's 429 rules never reach the page. The same class covers any future relay of a quota refusal (Orc's daily question cap when the AI opens, D1).

findings_seen.title: M481 'C3 gaps' (OPEN) confirmed: the 3a route walks are scoped by module and path, so a new principal-only content route (3e examples, a 3c relay outside /api/terminal/v1) is reported by no walk
findings_seen.general_class: A capability walk scoped by module or path instead of by the whole route table. Any new module, path family or tab (examples, the cut relay, Phase 4 admin routes, Phase 5 payment routes) escapes it.

findings_seen.title: M481 'C3 gaps' (OPEN) confirmed: the SSE monitor.view re-check works but no test holds it, and a TestClient cannot test it
findings_seen.general_class: Behaviour of long-lived answers (SSE, streamed relays) tested through Starlette TestClient, which buffers the whole stream: the re-check of a stream and the cut-off of a running relay need a live-server test (as test_auth_pages_live.serve does).

findings_seen.title: The session's access.limits reports the plan's raw value, not the min(plan, HARD) every route applies
findings_seen.general_class: A limit reported in two places, the session's access.limits and each route's own limits() or limit field, from two computations. The same holds for any future capped limit that the page reads via limit(key) instead of its route.

findings_seen.title: D5 second path: the account preferences route serves and stores tab content (Backtest 'My metrics' ml.my, the Screener's last screen scr.last) without that tab's capability
findings_seen.general_class: A per-user store that is not a tab's own route (preferences, or any later generic store) carries a tab's saved items, so the tab's read and save capabilities do not cover them.

findings_seen.title: 3c design gaps on the code it builds on: Terminal data limits bind only the Terminal paths, and PageFiles' owner-free shared caches conflict with per-owner headers, usage and audit
findings_seen.general_class: A data restriction enforced on one path (the Terminal proxy) while other tabs read the same data through their own workers or files, and owner-free shared caches placed in front of a call that becomes per owner.

findings_seen.title: F1: no route reads the capability screener.preset, so the Screener catalog lists presets (with their counts) that the plan does not hold
findings_seen.general_class: A catalog capability that a migration seeds and documents, but that no route reads: a gate promised by the catalog and never enforced. Same class in the seed: terminal.compare and terminal.assets have 0 reads in apps/edge-bff (server or page). terminal.dataset, terminal.tickers and terminal.history_days have 0 reads until 3c, and the <tab>.example flags until 3e. 3c and 3e should each list which seeded capability they make readable. A test should fail on a seeded capability with no reader that is not on an explicit 'later phase' list.

findings_seen.title: F2: the workers hard-code their own capability family in CAPABILITY_REQUIRED, but the 3b follow-up (built with 3c) moves the indicator and Flow grants to terminal.* and deletes the backtest.*/screener.* rows
findings_seen.general_class: Two services name the same decision separately: edge-bff decides the grant, the worker names it in its refusal, and nothing binds the two. The same mechanism applies wherever a refusal is produced by a service other than the one that owns the catalog. In 3c that is terminal-api refusing with terminal.dataset:<id>, terminal.history_days or terminal.tickers, built from a header edge-bff sends. In later tabs it is Orc's refusals when the AI opens to plans. Each needs a cross-service test that the named capability is a live catalog row and the one the decision was made by.

findings_seen.title: F-msg: the workers' CAPABILITY_REQUIRED message carries the internal capability key, and every EDGE page shows the server's message to the person
findings_seen.general_class: A message for the person is written by a service other than edge-bff and relayed verbatim, bypassing edge-bff's wording rules (display names, no internal keys). The same path exists for every worker refusal relayed as is (CONDITION_RESTRICTED, LIMIT_EXCEEDED) and for 3c's terminal-api refusals that edge-bff will relay (locked datasets, the history cut). Either the producer words them for people or edge-bff replaces the message from code and details.

findings_seen.title: O3b-2 variant: values shown in every result row and in /universe stay gated by id as conditions (chg_1d_pct, never named in O3b-2; and the page's own extra-columns anchor 'bars gt 0' needs screener.metric:bars)
findings_seen.general_class: A gate by id on a value that another answer of the same tab serves ungated (rows, /universe), and a page-built condition that silently depends on an item grant. The same check applies to 3c (a dataset locked in /bundle but present inside another file such as the reference list or a pack) and to the Overview and Watchlist files.

findings_seen.title: Terminal data limits (tickers, datasets, history_days, quotas) bind only the /api/terminal/v1 path: the Backtest and Screener workers read everything with their own service keys, and the Backtest page reads the Terminal route itself
findings_seen.general_class: Plan limits defined for one tab's data path, while other tabs reach the same data through service accounts (workers) or through that tab's route (the Backtest and Watchlist pages). This is the cross-tab coupling of ERRORS M481 C2 1 in reverse: a tab silently needs another tab's capabilities and limits. It applies to 3c (every terminal.* limit), the Watchlist and Overview pages, and the AI when it opens to plans.

findings_seen.title: Flow values outside the flow gate: the Overview and Watchlist page files carry every stock's foreign net (broker data), gated only by overview.view and watchlist.view
findings_seen.general_class: Publisher page files bundle values of a gated kind into one shared file per tab (the M476 class), so an item gate cannot reach them. This applies to 3d and to any future flow or custom indicator added to a page file.

findings_seen.title: The Screener page's boot cache paints the last result and catalog of an earlier plan after a narrowing: the pointer is keyed by login and data versions, not the entitlements version
findings_seen.general_class: Client caches of item-dependent answers keyed by data version instead of the principal's version (X-Edge-Entitlements). The same check applies to the Backtest page's results and any page keeping answers in IndexedDB or localStorage. 3c's Terminal file cache is safe by sha (the cut has its own sha).

findings_seen.title: CI never runs the shared session module's tests (Terminal vitest) or the account-page browser tests; a sign-out that keeps the account's data (M473 regression) passes every CI job
findings_seen.general_class: Suites that exist but are wired into no workflow: apps/edge-bff/terminal (34 files), overview, radar and watchlist page tests (2 files each), and every Playwright test of edge-bff (149, among them the M471 front-end contract and the account pages). Any later tab change (3e lock prompts, 3f lab chunk, the Terminal's handling of 3c's locked datasets and cut files) lands in these untested-in-CI suites.

findings_seen.title: market-ai-orc's conversation-ownership tests (incl. the Phase 0 C2 CLIENT-history fix) are skipped in CI; removing the fix leaves the Orc job green
findings_seen.general_class: Every Postgres-backed Orc test (372 skipped in CI): conversation ownership (test_another_owner_cannot_continue_or_read_a_conversation), branch lineage per owner, export ownership (test_export.py:115). The same mechanism (a suite needing a service CI does not start) applies to any future owner-isolation test placed in those files.

findings_seen.title: Column-level privileges pass every grant guard: the $verify$ blocks, provision_edge_bff_login.py and the apply-job probes check has_table_privilege only
findings_seen.general_class: Every grant guard in the repository built on has_table_privilege: all edge_bff $verify$ blocks (20261008_002 onwards), the provisioning script, the apply-job probes, and the market-ai reader roles' checks; 3c's new grants (terminal.subscriber column, the edge_bff quota rows) will copy the same pattern.

findings_seen.title: admin_audit is rewritten by user deletion: its FKs are ON DELETE SET NULL, so the hourly pending-account purge nulls the target of audit rows
findings_seen.general_class: Provenance columns with ON DELETE SET NULL: user_capability_overrides.created_by_user_id (20261117_003:80) loses who granted an override; Phase 5 payment_events and any audit-like table referencing users will hit the same mechanism.

findings_seen.title: A change of the plan catalog leaves no trace: plan_capabilities.updated_at and version are not maintained on UPDATE, and overrides have no updated_at/updated_by
findings_seen.general_class: Operator-edited data tables without an update trigger or audit: plans, capabilities, plan_capabilities, user_capability_overrides, subscriptions (last_event_at only); 3c adds its Terminal quota rows to plan_capabilities.

findings_seen.title: static/edge-session.js (the shell's copy of the session module) is compared with its build by no CI job; the generated-file rule misses build-shell.mjs
findings_seen.general_class: Generated files whose generator sits outside a `scripts` folder; header-only freshness checks.

findings_seen.title: Records contradict themselves or the decisions: M468-M475 say OPEN/not deployed under 'deployed' headings; the live capabilities.kind comment says wrong shapes are 'ignored'; terminal.history_days means 'back from today' against D2
findings_seen.general_class: Live database comments and seed texts frozen in applied migrations; ERRORS headings grown by appending.

findings_seen.title: Three database backstops no test locks: users_registration_pending, the email-code attempts cap, users_one_seed
findings_seen.general_class: Defence-in-depth constraints duplicated in application code.
